title: Prescription Insurance on File — Secondary Billing Settings by Plan Class
content:
Where a patient has two plans on file under **Prescription Insurance on File**, three class-level settings govern secondary billing: whether the class may be billed as the secondary payer at all, whether the class is always billed after every other coverage, and how long after the primary claim the secondary claim may be billed.

| Plan class | May be billed as secondary | Payer of last resort | Secondary billing window (calendar days after the primary claim) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Medicaid Managed Care Pharmacy Benefit | Yes | Yes | 365 |
| Medicare Part D Standard Plan | Yes | No | 90 |
| Medicare Part D Enhanced Plan | Yes | No | 90 |
| Medicare Advantage Prescription Drug Plan | Yes | No | 90 |
| Commercial High-Deductible Health Plan | Yes | No | 90 |
| Commercial Copay Plan | Yes | No | 90 |
| Workers' Compensation Pharmacy Benefit | No | No | 0 |

## Terms used

- **May be billed as secondary** — whether this plan class may be billed as the secondary payer.
- **Payer of last resort** — whether this plan class is always billed after every other coverage.
- **Secondary billing window** — calendar days after the primary claim within which the secondary claim may be billed.

## Notes

- The Medicaid Managed Care Pharmacy Benefit is the only payer of last resort and has the longest secondary billing window, 365 days.
- The Workers' Compensation Pharmacy Benefit may not be billed as secondary; its window is shown as 0.
